title: the ball keeps the tambora
story: Rompecintura at 152.3 BPM, a merengue break: the approach (7669-7870) is the full groove, the rings turn slowly and the ball, thrown from the centre on each round, hits ring 0 once per beat (impulso 0.741, the wall at 0.146 crosses in one beat), so the wall hits land on the beat of the tambora. The guira strokes shake the picture on alternating 8ths, the tambora's low strokes pull the zoom back and lift the brightness, and the palette sways every half bar. At the break (7870, RMS -3.6 sd) the drums drop out: the ball's speed steps down, the hits spread to two beats apart and the stack barely turns, so the mechanism stays readable. On the relaunch at 7933 (onset 12.75) the flash fires and the ball is thrown twice as fast (impulso 1.48): its wall hits fall on the 8ths, and the post-roll carries the drums bar after bar with the ball landing on the tambora.
